reviewer: outdoor_pool assistant subagent; rooftop implementation contributor performing separate current-image inspection, not blinded external validation.
review_method: Opened every capture listed by the current 42-PASS direct_roof_gpu report: 7 PNGs, including both deck exits and direct arrival, after the final pool-shortcut camera UI branch rerun. No runtime source edits, avatar/camera overrides, image edits or engine execution during this review.

distinguished_evidence.direct_jump_access: The automated report observes71 fresh Space presses, original-street ascent to94.972m and actual landing on the shared roof with visit_active=false and player_interior_active=false; stills show the resulting rendered facility, not the full ascent by themselves.
distinguished_evidence.water_and_both_exits: Current stills show splash, visible buoyant avatar and clear post-exit bodies; physical movement/support/entry/exit comes from the referenced automated observations.
distinguished_evidence.outside_departure: The report records leaving the actual source footprint and landing outside with no recovery or lift and with water unregistered. No separate final street-departure still is present, so that conclusion is report-derived rather than visually certified here.
distinguished_evidence.bounded_mode: This direct-jump journey uses exterior mode. It does not validate free-roam-OFF roof bounds, cabin rollback or catalog-wide landings; separate reports below carry those regressions.
distinguished_evidence.lift_reentry: The E prompt is visible in the direct-arrival frame. Actual E adoption/reboarding behaviour belongs to the separate direct_lift_h regression, not this still.

images.name: hotel_pool_normal_arrival
observed: The visible original avatar stands on the shared roof with a broad flush pool ahead after direct street-to-roof jumping.
The lift enclosure is present and its E floor-selection prompt is visible even though no elevator was used to arrive.
Skyline, coping and open water establish the outdoor roof location.
limitations: This capture name is inherited: in this report it is direct-jump arrival, not an elevator-arrival screenshot.
The general outdoor controls panel plus rooftop hint is taller than the compact lift-session HUD.
A source building label intrudes at the left water edge and the E prompt covers part of the lower legs.
The recorded 30-tick settle includes 2 initial hidden-avatar ticks near LiftRear; the inspected capture is clear with 29 meshes and settled distance 3.049m.

images.name: jump_above_flush_pool
observed: The existing avatar is fully visible above the coping; a large long-axis water surface, lane markings and outdoor leisure furniture are visible.
The roof facility is rendered without first entering a lift-only region.
limitations: Simple low-poly furniture and water remain game-authored.

images.name: splash_on_physical_entry
observed: A droplet cluster and ring appear around the visible torso while entering the real water area.
The pool edge and distant loungers/parasols remain visible.
limitations: An entry handrail crosses the lower foreground without hiding the head/torso.
A building name label floats over part of the far water/deck edge in this exterior mode.

images.name: buoyant_swimming_in_sunken_basin
observed: The original head and upper torso stay above water, with the legs visible below the translucent surface.
Open sky and the leisure deck remain visible during the swim.
limitations: Near-entry rail foreground and a floating source building label remain noticeable.
The clothed upright avatar indicates game buoyancy rather than a finished swim stroke.

images.name: large_open_sky_swimming_pool
observed: The avatar is centred and unobstructed in a wide water rectangle with visible lane strips, open sky and far leisure deck.
No foreground rail dominates the central swimming view.
limitations: The panel still combines general exploration and roof instructions; detailed swim/material realism is outside this review.

images.name: Space_exit_back_on_deck
observed: The original avatar is fully visible on the clear deck strip after the actual Space exit.
Loungers and parasols no longer force the camera to collapse or hide the body.
limitations: This frame looks toward furniture and adjacent simplified roof envelopes, not a surveyed hotel panorama.

images.name: Space_exit_right_back_on_deck
observed: The original avatar is fully visible on the opposite deck strip after Space exit, with the skyline beyond the glass edge.
The pool coping and walking strip remain legible without facility props hiding the player.
limitations: This outward view does not show the leisure furniture; it is a second exit/camera view, not a full facilities overview.

remaining_limits: Direct arrival reports 2 initially hidden-avatar ticks near LiftRear during a 30-tick settle. Final frame has 29 visible avatar meshes, first camera distance 1.560m and settled 3.049m; do not describe this as zero transient occlusion.
Exterior mode keeps the taller general-help-plus-roof HUD and source building labels; these are less clean than the compact elevator-session HUD.
The near-entry handrail occupies the lower foreground in two water frames without hiding the head/torso.
The original clothed upright low-poly avatar and simple water remain; finished strokes, swimwear, wet materials and fluid simulation are unverified.
The selected representative Plaza images do not validate every source roof, every camera orientation or a human OS-input journey.
The elevated game deck and sunken water geometry remain authored facilities above unchanged source slabs, not a real hotel-roof/pool survey.
